title: exec addressed a sandbox's host key by its bare name, so a second group's copy failed
foundBy: session agent, walking README.md and INSTALL.md as a first-time reader

evidence.verified: Reproduced on this host with README walkthrough 8: exec of api.cache-redis then api.cache-memory, the second exiting 255 on Host key verification failed. After the change, TestSSHArgsKeysHostKeyOnTheObjectName asserts the alias for three groups and the unset one, and fails on the previous code with `HostKeyAlias "api", want "api.default"`.

details:
README walkthrough 8 creates `api` and `bench` in two groups, then runs:

```
cs-sandbox exec api.cache-redis  pwd
cs-sandbox exec api.cache-memory pwd
```

The second command exits 255 with "REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED". `internal/engine/firecracker.go` passed `HostKeyAlias=<name>` to ssh, dropping the group, so both sandboxes shared the entry `api` in `~/.ssh/known_hosts.cs-sandbox` and the second presented a different key for it. Under `BatchMode=yes` there is nobody to accept it.

`hostcfg.Ref` already documents the invariant: the object name is "a sandbox's canonical, always-unambiguous ssh alias". The generated ssh config and `forward` both kept it. `exec`, `cs-sandbox ssh` and the `fetch`/`push` transport did not.

The podman engine was never affected: `podman.Exec` addresses the container as `<name>.<group>` and says why.
